newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end lower, waiting on the Fed.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end lower, waiting on the Fed.

text.p: French shares closed with losses on Monday, as the market took a cautious view ahead of Tuesday's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting, traders said.
Markets are adjusting to a quarter percent pre-emptive rise in U.S. rates but investors were unwilling to commit themselves until a move is confirmed. French bonds were steady.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 7.85 points or 0.3 percent, at 2,579.28. The CAC-40 futures contract was down eight at 2,580 from Friday's close.
Volume was a light 4.8 billion francs.
* Lyonnaise des Eaux rose, Suez fell.

Rumours of a merger between the two firms grip the market. "The market is betting on the fact that the merger will take place and that Suez will absorb Lyonnaise des Eaux, which means Suez will have to pay a premium to encourage that merger," a trader said.
The two firms' shares had risen sharply in the morning on reports a merger deal would be drafted in time for a presentation to the Suez board meeting on April 1.
* Essilor flat at 1,500 and Promodes slips 0.21 percent at 1,862, after research consultancy Detroyat adds the stocks to its big capitalisations list.
* Credit Lyonnais slips 0.49 percent to 203 francs. Dupont-Denant revised 1997 profit forecast to 1.3 billion francs from 400 million and 1.6 billion from 800 million for 1998.
* Rexel ends 3.41 percent higher at 1,758. The market welcomed news of three acquisitions made last Friday.

* Near-term support was seen at 2,575 on the CAC and below that the 2,550 area, which some see as a buying opportunity. "The market is still too expensive," said one broker, who thought prices could fall if the Fed raises rates tomorrow.
* Another market operator thought prices could rise if the U.S. tightening were limited to a quarter percent.
